clue.text: Masses of salt water around motorway — lock sewer

indicators.note: the bodies of salt water are wrapped about the motorway letter, which sits inside them

parts.note: seas are great masses of salt water
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A grim scene of oceans, a motorway and a sewer lock, like a civil-engineering report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, but here it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who stitches clothes for a living is someone who sews, so a sewer in that sense.

clue.text: Soft drink if you don't mind — just a half

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips

indicators.note: only the front half of the polite phrase's synonym is kept

parts.note: a polite request phrase, equivalent to please

explanation.surface: Someone politely asks for just a half-pint of a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' looks like one phrase, but 'Soft' is the definition alone; PLE is half of PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means pliant and bendy, which is a sense of soft.

clue.text: Exact retribution for raven getting caught

indicators.note: the letters are held captive within the two words raven getting

explanation.surface: Someone seeks revenge on behalf of a captured raven.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact retribution for a wrong is to take revenge on its behalf, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Aren't car bits ordered? I forget

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled motorist cannot remember whether the car parts were ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I forget' is what a forgetful, disorganised person typically says, so it serves as an example definition.

clue.text: Help to support Republican attack

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Political aid is given to back a Republican offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault or attack on a place.

clue.text: Reconcile this writer with a large, satisfying feast

parts.note: to square things is to reconcile them, as in squaring accounts
the setter referring to themselves gives me
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: The writer makes peace over a big, filling banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A square meal is an idiom for a substantial, filling meal.

clue.text: Stare at internet search engine, losing energy

indicators.note: the search engine's name drops the letters for energy

parts.note: Google is the best-known internet search engine
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at a search engine page, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy' suggests the single letter E, but here it is GO.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone, usually with desire.

clue.text: Group of men heading for George Harrison leaving hotel

indicators.note: the front letter of the name George is taken
the hotel letter departs from the surname

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A band of men heads off as Beatle George Harrison checks out of his hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of troops stationed in a fort or town.

clue.text: Greene's novel keeping one's fire up

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold another letter inside them
novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Graham Greene novel holds a reader's passion and fires them up.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to invigorate or stir into action, the same as to fire someone up.

clue.text: Like a moneylender perhaps, before father almost gets caught with debts

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the father word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: dad is father
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A loan shark's story: an ancestor nearly caught with unpaid debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Predacious means predatory, which a grasping lender might be thought, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Genuine ceasefire, though not constant

indicators.note: the word for a ceasefire goes without the constant's letter

parts.note: a truce is a ceasefire
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light in physics

explanation.surface: A real ceasefire, though one that might not last.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine are synonyms meaning real or authentic.

clue.text: Gossip as flier let out story about motorbike races

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, something that flies

indicators.note: out signals the three letters are put out of order
the story word goes around the race letters

parts.note: a tale is a story
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorbike races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A bird set free tells a yarn about motorcycle racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is idle chatter or rumour, a synonym of gossip.

clue.text: Smooth limb before tattoo oddly removed

indicators.note: the limb comes ahead of the remaining letters

parts.note: a leg is a limb

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word are taken away, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A limb is smoothed out after a tattoo is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction for playing notes smoothly and connected.

clue.text: Showering after little time exercising

indicators.note: the weather word follows the short time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
showering means raining

explanation.surface: A quick shower after a short workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showering' looks like washing, but it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is physical exercise done to build fitness, so it means exercising.

clue.text: Connected case to said criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A court case is linked to a crook who spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Associated means linked or joined together, a synonym of connected.

clue.text: Sum up posture: worryingly cocky

indicators.note: a worrying rearrangement of the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone sums up another's swaggering posture as alarmingly arrogant.
explanation.definitionFit: Presumptuous means overconfident and taking liberties, close to cocky.

clue.text: Uninterested, having no catalogue?

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
the suffix -less means having no, as in hopeless

explanation.surface: A shopper is bored because the catalogue never arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the answer split as LIST-LESS, 'having no catalogue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy or enthusiasm, so uninterested.

clue.text: Mark on church left by Yankee? Not at all

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
CE is the Church of England
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Was the church marked by an American? Certainly not.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly and barely shade into 'not at all', as in 'I could scarcely refuse'.

clue.text: Joined in with business deals, initially

parts.note: corporate means relating to a business corporation

indicators.note: the first letter of the word deals is taken

explanation.surface: Someone got involved in some business transactions early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorporated means combined into a whole, so joined together.

clue.text: Is climbing before slip up on a mountain range

indicators.note: the turned word precedes the rest
in a down entry, climbing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to err is to slip up or make a mistake

explanation.surface: A climber slips while ascending a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged chain of mountains, as in the Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Marriage partner going round lake — something of interest to a groom?

definitions.text: something of interest to a groom?

indicators.note: the partner word circles the lake letter

parts.note: a bride is a partner in a marriage

explanation.surface: A bride walks around a lake, which naturally interests her groom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' seems to be the bridegroom, but the definition means a stable groom.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable groom tends horses and their tack, and a bridle is the headgear for a horse.

clue.text: Petrified with editor wanting chapter to be brilliant

indicators.note: the word wanting a chapter means its editor letters are swapped for that letter

parts.note: petrified means terrified

explanation.surface: A frightened editor needs a chapter to be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with editor wanting chapter' says ED, at the end of TERRIFIED, gives way to C.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrific in its informal sense means excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Blow that is by king's sword

parts.note: a rap is a sharp blow
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king's sword delivers a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a thin, light sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: Payment by learner makes sense

parts.note: a fee is a payment
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Charging a student a fee is a sensible idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes sense' looks like one phrase; only 'sense' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel is to perceive by touch, one of the senses, so it means to sense.

clue.text: Just the first lady and Biden, finally

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: the last letter of the name Biden

explanation.surface: Simply the First Lady and President Biden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first lady' suggests the President's wife, but it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and just both mean fair or equitable, as in an even-handed ruling.

clue.text: Standing way to the left of Conservative radical

indicators.note: in an across entry the street word sits before the others

parts.note: a street is a way or road
red means politically radical or left-wing

explanation.surface: A political radical stands left of the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility among young people, a kind of standing or status.

clue.text: Place for pigs by river

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
x means by, as in measurements like 3 x 4

explanation.surface: A pigsty located beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but gives X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Styx is the river of the underworld in Greek myth.

clue.text: Corrupt European is after X-rated lick

indicators.note: the European letter follows the X-rated word

parts.note: adult describes X-rated material
a lick is a speed, as in going at a fair lick, a rate

explanation.surface: A European seeks a bit of racy, X-rated action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lick' seems physical, but 'at a fair lick' means at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate is to make impure by adding inferior substances, so to corrupt.
